comments.body:
Implementation written in worktree `.rebar/worktrees/impl-e508` (branched from `origin/main` `0e7401446c5`). Not yet committed or pushed.

**AC1 — re-export identity.** New antipattern entry in `code-review-tests.md`, placed after `loc-ceiling-pinning`. Detection shape: the whole assertion is that a symbol is importable from or re-exported by a module (`from pkg import thing`, `hasattr`, `pkg.thing is impl.thing`, `importlib.import_module` + attribute lookup) with no call into the behaviour reached through it. Litmus: *once the import succeeds, does the test exercise anything?* FP guard in-entry: a re-export that is itself the declared contract — a documented compatibility alias, deprecation shim, or stable public entry point.

**AC2 — import shape.** Detection shape: asserting a module's import list, `__all__` contents, or import ordering instead of behaviour. Litmus: *does the assertion read the module's import/export declarations rather than call the module?* FP guard in-entry: a public-API surface census a NON-HUMAN consumer reads is the Rule-5 structural-boundary case. The entry states the distinction explicitly — consumer, not syntax.

**AC3 — gate-script re-run.** Detection shape: invoking the project's own gate script (CI check, ratchet, policy scanner) over the real tree and asserting its verdict. The entry names both costs: it cannot fail independently of the gate CI already runs, and it ratifies whatever the gate currently reports, so it stays green when the gate's own baseline is wrong. FP guard in-entry: running the UNIT under test as a subprocess with a liveness anchor (guard (iii)), and calling the gate's own functions against a constructed fixture tree.

All three exemptions are also mirrored into the numbered FP guard list as (xii), (xiii), (xiv), matching how `f86e` added (xi).

**AC4 — eval corpus.** 6 cases appended to `code-review-tests.eval.yaml`, taking the dataset from 33 to 39. Each carries `corpus`, `expect`, `mode`, and a `note` naming the story, in the same shape as the `3fce` and `f86e` cases:

| id | expect | what it pins |
|---|---|---|
| `R-reexport-identity-only` | finding | `rebar.claim is impl` with nothing called through it |
| `FP-reexport-is-the-contract` | pass | same diff documents the alias as supported; test calls through and asserts the value |
| `R-importshape-all-literal` | finding | `__all__ == [...]` copied into the test, no consumer |
| `FP-importshape-generated-surface-census` | pass | live surface compared against the generated manifest a tool writes |
| `R-gatererun-subprocess-verdict` | finding | shells out to `check_complexity_baseline.py --check` over the real tree |
| `FP-gatererun-fixture-tree` | pass | calls `compare()` against a constructed baseline |

**AC6 — routing comment.** `criteria_routing.json`'s `tests._comment` now records all three additions, names the guards (xii)-(xiv), and names both homes (detection language in `reviewers/code-review-tests.md`, corpus in `eval_specs/code-review-tests.eval.yaml`) with the full case-prefix list. It closes with "No threshold or applies_to change." — `block_threshold` stays 0.54, `blocking_enabled` stays true, `applies_to` is untouched.

Verified so far: the JSON and YAML both parse, and all 6 new case ids are present in the loaded dataset.

**Not yet done:** AC5 (eval scores at or above its recorded pass bar) and AC7 (`make verify` exits 0). Both are blocked on host capacity rather than on the change — load average is 54 on a 6-core box with four concurrent `make verify` runs from other agent sessions.

comments.body:
AC5 route determined, plus a bug found while determining it.

**The live eval is runnable locally**, and that is the established evidence route: ticket 4569-8552-6c7e-4610 recorded a full live score from `rebar.llm.evals.eval.run_eval(...)`, "the same call the prompt-eval live CI job makes". `rebar prompt eval <id>` is offline-only (validate + summarize); there is no case filter on any surface, so AC5 costs a full 39-case x 3-epoch run (117 case-runs). CI caps at `REBAR_EVAL_MAX_CASES: "12"` and so never scores the tail of the dataset where this story's 6 new cases sit — a local full run is the only thing that scores them.

Offline validation of the edited spec passes:

```
Eval spec for prompt 'code-review-tests': VALID
  epochs=3  gate=at_least(2)  coverage>=0.8
  gating (deterministic): ['code_review_emits_valid_findings', 'code_review_recall', 'code_review_no_fire']
  dirty prompt sha256: 422ab14e833343ec...
```

The run evaluates the DIRTY working-tree prompt (`_llm_eval_commands.py:60` — "The DIRTY working-tree prompt is what an eval would evaluate (WS-G1)"), so this story's uncommitted rubric entries are what gets scored. Local gate-source mode is required for the same reason: an attested snapshot would score `origin/main` and miss the new entries entirely.

**Bug found:** the first attempt returned `coverage=0.0, epoch_pass=[false,false,false]` in 40 seconds, with all 117 case-runs carrying one identical error — `run_eval` must execute inside `rebar.llm.gate_source.gate_read_root`. The CI job calls it unwrapped and sets no override, so the live eval corpus has not been scoring anything since the raze-vet-ditch safeguard landed, and `continue-on-error: true` makes total failure look like an ordinary advisory regression. Filed as bug 77b6-868f-f4bd-461f (dissocial-unpleasant-adouri), linked `discovered_from` this story. Not remediated here — out of scope for this story's ACs.

The scoring run for AC5 is now in flight inside a local-mode gate session. Result to follow.

comments.author: Rebar Bot
comments.body:
AC5 measured against a baseline. The spec's gate was ALREADY red on main before this story, and the cause sits outside this story's three antipattern families.

Both runs are full 3-epoch, no case cap, local-mode gate session, on the dirty working tree.

| Run | Cases | Distinct failing | coverage | epoch_pass | elapsed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline (`origin/main`, this story's 3 files reverted) | 33 | 6 | 1.0 | `[false,false,false]` | 2027.9s |
| With this story | 39 | 5 | 1.0 | `[false,false,false]` | 2626.2s |

**All 6 of this story's new cases passed in all 3 epochs** — `R-reexport-identity-only`, `FP-reexport-is-the-contract`, `R-importshape-all-literal`, `FP-importshape-generated-surface-census`, `R-gatererun-subprocess-verdict`, `FP-gatererun-fixture-tree`. The story's AC1-AC4 and AC6 deliverables are good.

Every failure in both runs is a PRE-EXISTING false-positive case from another antipattern family — LOC ceiling, Rule 5, deliberate tightening, pre-existing-gap, sleep. Per-epoch:

```
BASELINE  e0: 3 failing   e1: 4 failing   e2: 3 failing
E508      e0: 4 failing   e1: 3 failing   e2: 3 failing
```

No clean epoch in 6 measured. The failing SET shifts between runs, so this is intermittent over-firing, not a deterministic wrong guard: re-running the 7 implicated FP cases once each produced 0 findings on all 7.

**Why the gate cannot pass as configured.** `_gating_results` passes an epoch only if EVERY applicable case passes (`eval.py`). The dataset now holds 20 no-fire cases. The measured per-case false-fire rate is roughly 3.3/20 = 0.17 per epoch, so P(clean epoch) = 0.83^20 = about 0.02, and the gate needs 2 clean epochs of 3. At this false-fire rate the bar is unreachable regardless of what this story adds — which is consistent with it having gone unnoticed, because bug 77b6 means CI has not actually scored this spec since the raze-vet-ditch safeguard landed.

Rebased onto current `origin/main` b7c6ed6c834 (32 commits; none touch this story's 3 files, and the only `src/rebar/llm/` change is `workflow/lint.py`), so updating does not resolve it. Work committed as 4d153d4cc27.

AC5 is not being reinterpreted or waived. Driving the pre-existing false-fire rate down is the work that makes it pass, and that is calibration of antipattern families this story did not add. Filing it as its own ticket and blocking this story on it, so this story closes against a genuinely green spec.

comments.author: Rebar Bot
comments.body:
Correction to the previous comment: the sentence "re-running the 7 implicated FP cases once each produced 0 findings on all 7" is not supported. Those runs failed before reaching the model — the Bedrock backend had no AWS profile selected, so each `run_case` raised, and the harness recorded the error as a case with zero findings. Zero findings there means the call never happened, not that the reviewer stayed quiet.

Re-running the same diagnostic with `AWS_PROFILE=frontier` set, which is what the full eval runs had. Everything else in the previous comment stands: the baseline and e508 eval runs both scored normally (coverage 1.0, 2028s and 2626s), so their per-epoch failure counts are real measurements.

The per-case false-fire rate of roughly 0.17 therefore rests on the two full eval runs alone, and the claim that the over-firing is intermittent rather than a deterministic wrong guard is currently unsupported. The re-run decides it: repeated fires on the same case point at a specific guard to fix, scattered fires point at calibration.

comments.body:
## AC5 amended — eval execution descoped, replaced by an offline pairing check

**Operator scope call (2026-11-04):** *"evals are out of scope for the complexity
remediation work"* / *"Running an eval does not reduce complexity."* The original AC5
required a live `run_eval` scoring pass against a recorded bar. That is eval execution, so
it leaves this program.

This is not a shortcut to closing: the replacement is a deterministic check that fails
without this story's work, and the corpus AC4 ships stays available to the live
calibration pass whenever it runs.

### What AC5 now requires, and why that shape

Each of the three new antipattern kinds must carry **both** an `R-*` recall case and an
`FP-*` false-positive guard case. A kind with only a fire case measures recall while being
blind to the false fires its guard exists to prevent — and the pre-existing spec-level
balance check (`test_code_review_dataset_balanced`) is satisfied by any single fire/no-fire
pair anywhere in the 39-case corpus, so it cannot see a one-sided new kind.

### What the test deliberately does NOT assert

**No rubric prose.** The rubric's Rule-5 exception (`code-review-tests.md:97-103`) holds
that a grepped token is a real contract only if a non-human consumer branches on its exact
value, and that an LLM is not such a consumer. A test pinning the new entries' wording
would be the `change-detector` antipattern this very story extends. Asserting the taxonomy
by grepping the taxonomy would have violated it.

**Not `mode` values either**, for the same reason one level down: `eval.py:223` lists
`mode` in `metadata_keys` — the set of keys the reviewer never receives — and nothing
branches on its value. `expect` and `id` are the machine-read contract (`FIRE_EXPECTS` /
`NOFIRE_EXPECTS` select the scorer; the validator enforces id uniqueness), so the
assertions sit there.

### Evidence it is not vacuous

Replayed the same three assertions against `HEAD~1`'s spec (33 cases, pre-e508):

```
reexport:    R-*=0  FP-*=0  -> FAIL
importshape: R-*=0  FP-*=0  -> FAIL
gatererun:   R-*=0  FP-*=0  -> FAIL
```

All 3 parametrizations fail without this story's cases; all 3 pass with them.
`tests/unit/test_code_review_evals.py` — 29 passed.

### Scope boundary left intact

AC4 (authoring the corpus cases) is untouched and remains delivered. The descope removes
paying a model to *run* the corpus, not the act of authoring it.

Commit `e5f2b55b740`, `Change-Id: Iacb27398315f4a9e3b19f6c1e4d3371f4c56a039`. AC7
(`make verify`) is running now.

compiled_state.description:
## Context

Epic `77e3-28e2` AC4 requires the code-review `tests` criterion to carry a taxonomy
distinguishing behaviour tests from tests that pin **refactor mechanics, re-export
identity, LOC floors, import shape, or re-run a gate script** — five named kinds.

Story `f86e-b57b-008d-4652` delivered one of them (`loc-ceiling-pinning`). The taxonomy is
2 of 5.

## Measured at `origin/main` `0e7401446c5`

`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-tests.md` carries 11 antipattern entries:
`change-detector`, `tautological`, `over-mocking`, `under-mocking`, `source-grepping`,
`existence-only`, `non-gating test`, `unrealistic fault injection`,
`contract-contradicting assertion`, `fail-open oracle`, `loc-ceiling-pinning`.

Mapping AC4's five named kinds onto those entries:

| AC4 kind | Covered by | State |
|---|---|---|
| refactor mechanics | `change-detector` (":58" "would break on a behavior-preserving refactor") | covered |
| LOC floors | `loc-ceiling-pinning` (f86e) | covered |
| re-export identity | — | **absent** |
| import shape | — | **absent** |
| re-run a gate script | — | **absent** |

Case-insensitive counts over the rubric: `re-export` 0, `reexport` 0, `__all__` 0,
`import` 0, `gate script` 0, `re-run` 0, `rerun` 0. The three kinds are not named under any
synonym. `change-detector` subsumes them generically ("asserts an internal name, structure,
or intermediate state"), but AC4 requires the taxonomy to *distinguish* them, and a reviewer
given only the generic entry has no detection language for these three shapes.

## Why the verification route is the eval corpus, not a prose grep

AC4's "Checked by" clause names "an overlay test asserting the taxonomy text is present in
the criterion's rubric". The rubric's own Rule-5 structural-artifact exception (`:97-103`)
forbids exactly that test:

> Litmus: the grepped token is a real contract iff a NON-HUMAN consumer (a parser /
> validator / downstream grep / registry / CI runner that branches on the exact value)
> reads it. An LLM is NOT a non-human consumer — a prose/heading grep that merely guards
> the author's wording IS a change-detector.

Measured: nothing but the LLM reads this rubric's antipattern headings. `git grep` over
`src/ scripts/ tests/` finds the rubric referenced only by `criteria_routing.json` (a prose
`_comment`), by `eval_specs/*.yaml` (which carry the text as fixture diffs), and by its own
front matter. No parser branches on the entry names.

So a test asserting the taxonomy's wording would commit the change-detector antipattern the
rubric defines. The project has already established the substitute twice — the
`criteria_routing.json:112` `_comment` records it for both `3fce` (fail-open oracle) and
`f86e` (loc-ceiling-pinning):

> Detection language + FP guards live in reviewers/code-review-tests.md; calibration corpus
> in eval_specs/code-review-tests.eval.yaml (R-loc-ceiling-* / FP-loc-* cases).

This story follows that route: the taxonomy's correctness is demonstrated by calibration
cases that show it FIRES on real instances and does NOT fire on the lookalikes, which is a
stronger claim than its prose matching a fixed string.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 — `code-review-tests.md` carries a **re-export identity** antipattern entry:
      a test whose assertion is that a symbol is importable from, or re-exported by, a
      module (the identity of the re-export) rather than the behaviour reached through it.
      The entry names the detection shape and at least one false-positive guard.
- [ ] AC2 — it carries an **import shape** entry: a test asserting a module's import list,
      `__all__` contents, or import ordering rather than behaviour. Guard: a genuine
      public-API surface census that a non-human consumer reads is NOT this antipattern.
- [ ] AC3 — it carries a **gate-script re-run** entry: a test that invokes the gate script
      under test and asserts its output, duplicating the gate rather than exercising the
      unit. Guard: Rule-5 command-output greps with an established producer-liveness anchor
      remain valid.
- [ ] AC4 — `eval_specs/code-review-tests.eval.yaml` gains recall cases (`R-reexport-*`,
      `R-importshape-*`, `R-gatererun-*`) and false-positive guard cases
      (`FP-reexport-*`, `FP-importshape-*`, `FP-gatererun-*`) for each new entry,
      matching the naming convention the `3fce` and `f86e` cases use.
- [ ] AC5 — a deterministic, OFFLINE test validates the six new corpus cases on the
      machine-read contract the eval loader actually enforces: each of the three kinds
      contributes exactly one `expect: finding` case and one `expect: pass` case (a kind
      with no no-fire case cannot measure false fires), every new case id is unique and
      follows the established `R-*` / `FP-*` convention, and every new case carries a
      non-empty `diff` — a key OUTSIDE the loader's metadata set (`eval.py:223`), so the
      reviewer receives real input rather than a case that silently scores on nothing.
      The test runs no model and makes no network call, mirroring sibling 39bc's
      `tests/unit/test_project_net_mechanism_eval.py`.

      The test deliberately asserts NOTHING about the rubric's prose. The rubric's Rule-5
      exception treats a prose/heading grep whose only consumer is the LLM as the
      `change-detector` antipattern — the family this very story extends — so a test
      pinning the new entries' wording would violate the taxonomy it ships. `mode` is
      excluded for the same reason: `eval.py:223` classes it as metadata the reviewer
      never receives, and nothing branches on its value.

      Scope note (operator decision, 2026-11-04): this REPLACES the original AC5, which
      required a live `run_eval` scoring pass against a recorded bar. Evals are out of
      scope for the complexity-reduction program on the stated grounds that running an
      eval does not reduce complexity. The live calibration pass is not abandoned — it is
      not this program's gate, and the corpus this story ships remains available to it.
- [ ] AC6 — `criteria_routing.json`'s `_comment` records the three additions in the same
      form it records `3fce` and `f86e`, naming where detection language and corpus live.
      No threshold or `applies_to` change.
- [ ] AC7 — `make verify` exits 0.

## Portability and provider neutrality

The deliverable is rubric prose plus eval-corpus cases. Nothing reads a CI environment, so
this behaves identically with no CI provider configured. No vendor or model-specific
capability is named, and the entries are detection language the reviewer applies regardless
of which provider backs the gate.

## Out of scope

- Changing the `tests` criterion's threshold or posture (already blocking at 0.54).
- Amending epic 77e3's AC4 "Checked by" clause — that is the epic's own edit, justified by
  the Rule-5 evidence above, and is not this story's deliverable.
- The other two AC4 kinds, which are already covered.

file_impact.reason: AC1-AC3: adds the re-export identity, import shape, and gate-script re-run antipattern entries plus FP guards (xii)-(xiv)
AC4: adds R-reexport-*/FP-reexport-*, R-importshape-*/FP-importshape-*, R-gatererun-*/FP-gatererun-* calibration cases
AC6: records the three additions in the tests criterion _comment; no threshold or applies_to change
AC5: offline per-kind pairing check — each new antipattern kind must carry both an R-* recall case and an FP-* guard case. Reads the spec YAML; runs no model.
